deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from the previous page, 'Geometrische Seite der ternären Formen'). Three non-coplanar vectors t, t', t'' issue from an origin 0. (u,v) is the scalar product. A point is P = x t + x' t' + x'' t''. The Gram matrix is G = [[a, b'', b'], [b'', a', b], [b', b, a'']], with a = (t,t), b = (t',t''), etc. Its adjugate is adj G = [[A, B'', B'], [B'', A', B], [B', B, A'']], with A = a'a'' - b^2, B = b'b'' - ab, etc. D = det G = squared volume of the parallelepiped on t, t', t''. Gauss writes ternary forms as (a, a', a''; b, b', b'').

(1) Reciprocal vectors. T = A t + B'' t' + B' t'', T' = B'' t + A' t' + B t'', T'' = B' t + B t' + A'' t''. In matrix form, (T, T', T'') = adj(G) applied to (t, t', t''). Hence (T_i, t_j) = (adj G · G)_ij = D δ_ij. So T is perpendicular to t' and t'', T' to t and t'', and T'' to t and t'. This is the marginal column 'senkrecht gegen'. In modern terms T = D t* = √D (t' × t''), where t* is the reciprocal (dual) basis; similarly for T' and T''.

(2) Normal to a plane. The plane is λX + λ'X' + λ''X'' = L in coordinates relative to t. For N = λT + λ'T' + λ''T'' one has (N, P) = D(λX + λ'X' + λ''X'') = DL, constant on the plane, so N is normal to it.

The boxed marginal note defines a quantity (written with a bold or decorated L, apparently distinct from the plane constant L): 'L = value of the adjoint form (A, A', A''; B, B', B'') at λ, λ', λ''.' It is used implicitly as follows (my filling): |N|^2 = λ^T adj(G) G adj(G) λ = D·F(λ), where F is the adjoint form. So the distance from 0 to the plane is DL / |N| = L √(D / F(λ)).

(3) Inversion. a T + b'' T' + b' T'' = D t, b'' T + a' T' + b T'' = D t', b' T + b T' + a'' T'' = D t''. This is G·adj(G) = D·I. Also (t, P) = a x + b'' x' + b' x'', (t', P) = b'' x + a' x' + b x'', (t'', P) = b' x + b x' + a'' x''. So t, t', t'' are normal to the planes on which these linear forms are constant.

(4) Triangle, pyramid, perpendicular. Take the triangle with vertices m t, m' t', m'' t''. Its doubled vector area is (m't' - mt) × (m''t'' - mt) = m'm'' t'×t'' + mm'' t''×t + mm' t×t' = (m'm'' T + mm'' T' + mm' T'') / √D (my step). Its squared length is D·F(X)/D = F(X), with X = m'm'', X' = mm'', X'' = mm'. So twice the area equals √F(m'm'', mm'', mm'), as Gauss states.

Six times the volume of the pyramid with apex 0 is mm'm''√D.

The perpendicular from 0 is 6V / (2·area) = mm'm''√D / √F(m'm'', mm'', mm'). Since F is quadratic, this equals √(D / F(1/m, 1/m', 1/m'')). This agrees with (2) for λ = 1/m, L = 1.

(5) Gram form of the reciprocal system. (T_i, T_j) = (adj G · G · adj G)_ij = D·(adj G)_ij. So T, T', T'' stand to the form (AD, A'D, A''D; BD, B'D, B''D), i.e. D times the adjoint form, as t, t', t'' stand to (a, a', a''; b, b', b''). This is the geometric meaning of Gauss's adjoint ternary form (Disq. Arith. art. 267): it is, up to the factor D, the Gram form of the reciprocal (polar) lattice.
errors: Third plane equation: the manuscript reads b'x + bx' + ax'' = Const; it must be b'x + bx' + a''x'' (missing primes, a slip).

The boxed marginal 'L = value of the adjoint form at λ, λ', λ''' reuses (or nearly reuses) the letter of the arbitrary plane constant L. It must denote a different quantity, F(λ) = |N|^2 / D; read literally it would conflict with the plane equation. Probably a distinct (bold/Fraktur) symbol.
No mathematical errors otherwise; all identities (adj G·G = D·I, area, volume, perpendicular, Gram matrix of the T's) check out.

results.what: T = adj(G)·t gives vectors with (T_i, t_j) = D δ_ij, i.e. T = √D (t'×t''), perpendicular to the other two edges
results.usually_credited_to: Bravais (1850), Gibbs (1881, vector analysis), Ewald (1913, crystallography)

results.what: Normal to the plane λX + λ'X' + λ''X'' = L is λT + λ'T' + λ''T''; its squared length is D times the adjoint form at λ
results.modern_name: normal vector via dual basis; the adjoint form as the metric on the dual space
results.usually_credited_to: standard analytic geometry / tensor calculus (raising indices with the inverse metric)

results.what: Twice the triangle area through m t, m' t', m'' t'' = √F(m'm'', mm'', mm'); perpendicular from 0 = √(D / F(1/m, 1/m', 1/m''))
results.modern_name: Gram-determinant area/volume formulas; distance from the origin to a lattice plane with intercepts m, m', m''
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange/Gauss-era analytic geometry; the lattice-plane spacing formula is standard in crystallography (19th c.)

results.what: Gram matrix of T, T', T'' equals D·adj(G): the adjoint ternary form is (up to D) the form of the reciprocal lattice
results.modern_name: polar/reciprocal lattice duality of quadratic forms
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Seeber review 1831, Nachlass), later Bravais, Hermite

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Gauss's notes on the geometric interpretation of ternary forms, connected with his 1831 Seeber review. To my knowledge these notes (and the crystallographic law on the next page) are printed in Werke II. Gauss's lattice interpretation and use of the adjoint form are well known. Having the reciprocal basis explicitly predates Bravais and Gibbs and is a nice detail, but it is not unknown.

transcription_corrections: Third plane equation: the manuscript indeed reads 'b'x + bx' + ax''' (Gauss's slip for a''x''); the transcription is faithful, but the slip should be flagged.
The boxed marginal 'L' is written in a heavier/different letter than the plane constant L; it likely denotes a distinct symbol (bold/Fraktur 𝔏).
'[-=-][?]' after the form is a struck-out scribble before '= F(m'm'', mm'', mm')' (the F-expression is written at the right end of the preceding line).
'der {+6fachen+} [-6fachen-] Pyramide': the original word was struck out and '6fachen' inserted above the line; the meaning is the 6-fold pyramid (= parallelepiped volume).
